## Coding scheme for transport blocks
Transport blocks ke liye TS 38.201 clause 4.2.3 kehta hai ki *quasi‑cyclic LDPC codes* use kiye jaate hain, jisme 2 base graphs aur har base graph ke liye 8 parity‑check matrix sets hote hain. 

## Coding scheme for PBCH
PBCH (Physical Broadcast Channel) aur control information ke liye same clause mein *Polar coding* ka zikr hai, jo nested sequences par based hota hai. 

## Analogy (sirf samjhane ke liye, standard ka text nahi)
Transport block coding ko aap ek *broadband cable* samajh sakte hain jo ek saath bahut saare data packets ko ek saath bhejta hai, isme LDPC ek *strong shield* ki tarah kaam karta hai jo errors ko detect aur correct karta hai. PBCH coding ko ek *dedicated radio station* ki tarah samjho jo sirf ek hi message (broadcast info) bhejta hai, aur Polar coding ek *special frequency tuning* ki tarah kaam karta hai jo ek hi message ko clear aur reliable banata hai.

## Exact citations
- Transport block coding: clause 4.2.3, sub‑clause *Channel coding* (TS 38.201 v18.0.0). 
- PBCH coding: clause 4.2.3, sub‑clause *Channel coding* (TS 38.201 v18.0.0).

cited_passages.passage_text:
4.2.3 Channel coding
The channel coding scheme for transport blocks is quasi-cyclic LDPC codes with 2 base graphs and 8 sets of parity
check matrices for each base graph, respectively. One base graph is used for code blocks larger than certain sizes or
with initial transmission code rate higher than thresholds; otherwise, the other base graph is used. Before the LDPC
coding, for large transport blocks, the transport block is segmented into multiple code blocks with equal size. The
channel coding scheme for PBCH and control information is Polar coding based on nested sequences. Puncturing,
shortening and repetition are used for rate matching. Further details of channel coding schemes are specified in [4].
